sources.title: Study guide for Exam AI-200: Developing AI Cloud Solutions on Azure
sources.shortSummary: The current undated AI-200 guide defines four weighted domains, nine skills, and 27 literal subskills. It establishes scope, not product behavior or GA status.

sources.title: Registries, repositories, and artifacts
sources.shortSummary: Distinguishes registry, repository, image manifest, mutable tag, and immutable digest addressing for container delivery.

sources.title: Build and run images with ACR Tasks
sources.shortSummary: Explains cloud build-and-push with az acr build, source/base-image/timer triggers, and multi-step build-test workflows.

sources.title: Tag and version images
sources.shortSummary: Contrasts reusable and unique deployment tags and describes locking deployed artifacts. Preview purge and retention features are excluded.

sources.title: Deploy containers to Azure App Service
sources.shortSummary: Describes private-image deployment, managed-identity registry pulls, image updates, and deployment verification.

sources.title: Configure container runtime behavior
sources.shortSummary: Explains container startup overrides, runtime port settings, persistence, and always-on tradeoffs. Confirm port defaults and health-check details against product documentation.

sources.title: Configure application settings
sources.shortSummary: Describes app settings as environment variables, typed connection-string prefixes, slot-specific configuration, and Key Vault references.

sources.title: Observe and troubleshoot containerized apps
sources.shortSummary: Uses container stdout/stderr, streaming logs, SCM diagnostics, and startup/configuration symptoms to troubleshoot container hosting.

sources.title: Explore Container Apps environments
sources.shortSummary: Explains the environment as a shared networking/logging boundary and distinguishes internal from external ingress.

sources.title: Deploy a container app using the Azure CLI and YAML
sources.shortSummary: Contrasts quick deployment with explicit environment-based deployment and versioned YAML configuration.

sources.title: Configure runtime settings with environment variables and secrets
sources.shortSummary: Separates ordinary environment values from app secrets and references secrets in runtime configuration without rebuilding images.

sources.title: Configure image pull authentication for private registries
sources.shortSummary: Explains private-registry authentication using managed identity versus stored credentials and inspecting registry configuration.

sources.title: Verify deployments with logs and status
sources.shortSummary: Uses app ingress, revision status, logs, and replica inventory to verify a deployment rather than assuming creation implies health.

sources.title: Update images and manage revisions safely
sources.shortSummary: Relates immutable image identity to revision-based rollout, multiple revision modes, rollback, and cleanup.

sources.title: Monitor logs and troubleshoot issues
sources.shortSummary: Uses revision-scoped logs and safe identifiers to isolate configuration, startup, and dependency failures without logging sensitive payloads.

sources.title: Configure health probes and troubleshoot failures
sources.shortSummary: Distinguishes readiness from liveness and uses probes plus revision logs to diagnose rollout failures.

sources.title: Configure scale rules
sources.shortSummary: Explains replica bounds, HTTP/TCP triggers, resource-based rules, and timing tradeoffs; specific defaults must match the product article.

sources.title: Implement event-driven scaling with KEDA
sources.shortSummary: Explains event-source metrics for KEDA scaling and distinguishes secret-based from supported managed-identity authentication.

sources.title: Apply KEDA scalers for custom workloads
sources.shortSummary: Describes translating ScaledObject trigger metadata/authentication into Container Apps rules and selecting custom event signals.

sources.title: Choose and apply revision modes
sources.shortSummary: Relates single/multiple revision modes, traffic weights, direct revision labels, and independent scaling of active revisions.

sources.title: Create Kubernetes deployment manifests
sources.shortSummary: Explains Deployment desired-state manifests, image references, replicas, resource requests/limits, and secret references; fixed replica recommendations are not guarantees.

sources.title: Expose applications in Azure Kubernetes Services
sources.shortSummary: Distinguishes Service port from targetPort and explains selector-to-Pod label matching and exposure choices.

sources.title: Deploy applications to Azure Kubernetes Services
sources.shortSummary: Uses kubectl apply and observed deployment, Pod, log, and endpoint state to distinguish successful submission from a working application.

sources.title: Define ConfigMaps for application settings
sources.shortSummary: Explains ConfigMap environment/file injection and immutable configuration objects used by AKS Deployment manifests.

sources.title: Implement secrets for sensitive data
sources.shortSummary: Describes Secret references in manifests and the separate CSI/Key Vault integration for centralized secret management.

sources.title: Monitor application logs and metrics
sources.shortSummary: Combines application logs, resource metrics, and Azure Monitor views to distinguish application and infrastructure signals.

sources.title: Troubleshoot pods and services
sources.shortSummary: Uses Pod events, previous logs, exec, and Service inspection to narrow pending, image-pull, and crash-loop failures.

sources.title: Verify service connectivity and endpoints
sources.shortSummary: Traces connectivity through Service selectors, endpoints, port-forwarding, and external load-balancer or ingress addresses.

sources.title: Implement the Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL SDK
sources.shortSummary: Explains CosmosClient reuse, resource clients, point reads requiring item ID and partition key, writes, and request-charge observation.

sources.title: Query Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL
sources.shortSummary: Covers parameterized SQL-style JSON queries, partition routing, projection, arrays, sorting, pagination, and RU inspection. Do not assume an unproven query-plan-cache benefit.

sources.title: Configure range and composite indexes
sources.shortSummary: Relates range/composite indexes to filters and multi-property ordering and notes the write cost and asynchronous index transformation.

sources.title: Tune vector indexes for embedding workloads
sources.shortSummary: Explains flat, quantizedFlat, and diskANN tradeoffs plus embedding-array range-index exclusions; use the current product article for exact limits.

sources.title: Reduce RU costs with strategic indexing
sources.shortSummary: Uses actual query patterns and RU metrics to prune unnecessary index paths and balance write cost against retrieval speed.

sources.title: Choose consistency levels for optimal performance
sources.shortSummary: Distinguishes consistency guarantees, session-token scope, and read-throughput tradeoffs. Search-index freshness is not implied by read-your-writes.

sources.title: Store and retrieve embeddings in Azure Cosmos DB
sources.shortSummary: Explains storing embeddings with content and metadata and configuring vector path, type, dimensions, and distance. The frozen training and product policies include float32, float16, int8, and uint8. Float16 can reduce the vectors' storage footprint with possible accuracy loss; workload-independent negligible-loss guarantees are not supported.

sources.title: Execute vector similarity queries for semantic search
sources.shortSummary: Uses matching embedding models, parameterized VectorDistance queries, bounded result counts, and distance-specific score interpretation.

sources.title: Combine vector similarity results with metadata filtering
sources.shortSummary: Combines vector retrieval with metadata and partition constraints. Hybrid/full-text and optimizer-placement claims require additional specific evidence.

sources.title: Use the change feed to trigger embedding refresh
sources.shortSummary: Explains lease/checkpoint coordination, idempotent embedding refresh, and Python pull-model versus Functions-trigger integration; the processor SDK itself is .NET/Java.

sources.title: Connect to PostgreSQL
sources.shortSummary: Covers connection parameters, secure transport, Entra/native authentication, and PgBouncer endpoint selection.

sources.title: Create and manage schemas
sources.shortSummary: Organizes relational schemas, constraints, metadata data types, and conventional indexes for AI application data.

sources.title: Query data
sources.shortSummary: Covers PostgreSQL metadata querying, keyset pagination, RETURNING, CTEs, and idempotent upsert patterns.

sources.title: Integrate SDKs and applications
sources.shortSummary: Uses psycopg integration, parameterized operations, connection reuse, asynchronous access, and transaction/error handling.

sources.title: Store and query embeddings with pgvector
sources.shortSummary: Covers pgvector enablement, dimensioned vector columns, embedding ingestion, and distance operators.

sources.title: Perform fast vector similarity search
sources.shortSummary: Contrasts exact search with IVFFlat/HNSW and requires matching query distance operators to index operator classes.

sources.title: Manage index lifecycle and embedding updates
sources.shortSummary: Covers index health, embedding refresh, model migration using separate columns, and storage maintenance; index maintenance must distinguish IVFFlat from HNSW.

sources.title: Run vector similarity search for semantic retrieval
sources.shortSummary: Combines similarity ranking with relational filters, distance thresholds, context projection, and optional hybrid retrieval.

sources.title: Implement retrieval patterns for RAG pipelines
sources.shortSummary: Structures documents/chunks for metadata-filtered retrieval and preserves source/chunk information for context and citations.

sources.title: Tune PostgreSQL for pgvector
sources.shortSummary: Explains vector distance compute cost, index memory pressure, planner inspection, and query-time accuracy/performance tuning.

sources.title: Choose and configure vector indexes
sources.shortSummary: Compares IVFFlat and HNSW construction/search tradeoffs and index maintenance. DiskANN is outside this curated pgvector scope.

sources.title: Optimize data layout
sources.shortSummary: Relates structured versus JSONB metadata, conventional filter indexes, table partitioning, and vector retrieval plans.

sources.title: Scale for high-volume workloads
sources.shortSummary: Relates compute/memory scale-up, read replicas, monitoring, and cache choices to measured vector workload bottlenecks.

sources.title: Connection optimization
sources.shortSummary: Explains connection churn, PgBouncer and application pools, transaction-local settings, batching, and resilient reconnection.

sources.title: Client libraries and development best practices
sources.shortSummary: Relates client support and same-slot multi-key constraints to Enterprise/OSS clustering, connection reuse, TLS, and pipelining.

sources.title: Implement data operations
sources.shortSummary: Covers cache-aside, TTL, explicit invalidation, and incremental SCAN. SETEX is string-specific; the unit's broad statement that SETEX works with all data types is excluded.

sources.title: Index and query vector data
sources.shortSummary: Defines vector schemas and KNN query fields/dimensions, dialect, metadata filtering, and serialized hash vectors.

sources.title: Choose vector types and indexing strategies
sources.shortSummary: Contrasts FLAT exact search with HNSW approximation and matches vector dimensions, types, and metrics to embeddings.

sources.title: Optimize Redis data structures for vector storage
sources.shortSummary: Contrasts binary vector fields in hashes with numeric arrays in JSON and the corresponding indexing/data-shape choices.

sources.title: Explore Azure Service Bus concepts and messaging in AI architectures
sources.shortSummary: Explains durable queues, load leveling, competing consumers, and temporal decoupling. Its exactly-once phrasing is not approved; settlement permits redelivery.

sources.title: Choose between queues and topics with subscriptions
sources.shortSummary: Distinguishes queue competition from per-subscription topic copies and broker-side property filtering. Processing exactly once is not guaranteed.

sources.title: Structure messages for AI workloads
sources.shortSummary: Distinguishes body/application/system properties, correlation identifiers, TTL, batching, and claim-check references; size maxima require tier/protocol qualification.

sources.title: Process messages reliably
sources.shortSummary: Covers explicit settlement, lock renewal, poison-message handling, and DLQ reprocessing. Expiry dead-lettering is conditional, not universally enabled.

sources.title: Understand Azure Event Grid concepts and event-driven patterns for AI solutions
sources.shortSummary: Separates event sources, topics, subscriptions, handlers, and state-change notifications from full resource payloads.

sources.title: Work with event schemas and properties
sources.shortSummary: Explains CloudEvents identity/data fields and type, subject, and typed advanced filters.

sources.title: Configure delivery and retry policies for reliable event processing
sources.shortSummary: Explains retry/TTL budgets, dead-letter storage, batching, and duplicate-safe handling. Not every error is retryable; use the product failure-code table.

sources.title: Publish custom events from AI applications
sources.shortSummary: Builds lightweight custom events and publishes with EventGridPublisherClient using an authorized identity rather than conflating authentication and publish permission.

sources.title: Understand Azure Functions hosting and scaling for AI workloads
sources.shortSummary: Relates hosting/cold starts, concurrency, and the HTTP response timeout to synchronous versus queued operations.

sources.title: Set up the local development environment for Functions
sources.shortSummary: Distinguishes function_app.py, host.json, local.settings.json, dependencies, Core Tools, and local/cloud configuration.

sources.title: Create triggers and bindings for AI integration patterns
sources.shortSummary: Explains one trigger per function, optional input/output bindings, HTTP/Service Bus patterns, and when direct SDK access is needed.

sources.title: Manage secrets and configuration in Functions
sources.shortSummary: Covers environment-based function settings, Key Vault references, and shared App Configuration rather than embedding secrets in code.

sources.title: Configure identity and access for Functions
sources.shortSummary: Distinguishes binding identity, direct SDK identity, and HTTP function authorization keys; a key is not caller identity.

sources.title: Store and organize secrets, keys, and certificates
sources.shortSummary: Distinguishes secret/key/certificate objects, vault organization, RBAC, and recovery protections.

sources.title: Retrieve secrets using Azure SDK client libraries
sources.shortSummary: Uses SecretClient to retrieve values or enumerate metadata with separate permissions and handles asynchronous access/errors.

sources.title: Handle secret versioning and rotation
sources.shortSummary: Describes secret version creation, rotation strategies, consumer refresh, and expiry metadata. The latest-enabled fallback assertion is excluded.

sources.title: Implement caching strategies to reduce Key Vault calls
sources.shortSummary: Balances in-memory secret caching, refresh-on-rotation, throttling, and backoff without treating cache TTL as credential revocation.

sources.title: Connect to App Configuration from application code
sources.shortSummary: Loads configuration through the Python provider with key/label selection, prefix trimming, identity, and explicit refresh.

sources.title: Organize settings with labels and feature flags
sources.shortSummary: Combines default and environment-labeled settings and distinguishes feature flag evaluation/refresh from ordinary settings.

sources.title: Reference Key Vault secrets from App Configuration
sources.shortSummary: Explains Key Vault reference metadata, independent service permissions, and secret refresh without storing secret values in App Configuration.

sources.title: Decide what to store in App Configuration vs Key Vault
sources.shortSummary: Places behavior settings in App Configuration and access-granting credentials in Key Vault while preserving complementary refresh/audit requirements.

sources.title: Explore OpenTelemetry and its role in observability
sources.shortSummary: Distinguishes traces, spans, propagation, and Azure Monitor terminology for distributed observation.

sources.title: Add the OpenTelemetry SDK to an application
sources.shortSummary: Installs the Python distro, configures ingestion, and separates services using resource attributes rather than merging all telemetry into one role.

sources.title: Configure spans and traces
sources.shortSummary: Creates custom/nested spans, attributes, status, and appropriate span kinds to represent distributed work.

sources.title: Export telemetry to Azure Monitor
sources.shortSummary: Explains export, consistent trace sampling, offline retries, and checking ingestion; rates and supported options require language/version context.

sources.title: Debug distributed flows with trace data
sources.shortSummary: Uses transaction waterfalls and KQL correlation to distinguish slow dependencies from local processing and trace gaps.

sources.title: Write basic KQL queries
sources.shortSummary: Uses KQL filtering, projection, grouping, aggregation, and chart rendering over telemetry tables.

sources.title: Explore logs for errors and performance
sources.shortSummary: Joins telemetry using operation identifiers and analyzes exception frequency, dependency latency, and failures within a declared table/query scope.

sources.title: Automate container image builds and maintenance with Azure Container Registry tasks
sources.shortSummary: Defines quick, triggered, and multi-step ACR Tasks, build contexts, and inspecting task output.

sources.title: Recommendations for tagging and versioning container images
sources.shortSummary: Recommends unique deployment tags versus stable base-image tags and protecting deployed tags from mutation.

sources.title: Configure a custom container for Azure App Service
sources.shortSummary: Documents runtime ports, injected environment variables, identity-based registry pulls, storage, and diagnostics for custom containers. Docker Compose preview sections are excluded.

sources.title: Update and deploy changes in Azure Container Apps
sources.shortSummary: Distinguishes revision-scope from application-scope changes, activation, traffic splitting, and zero-downtime single-mode rollover. Preview inactive-revision-limit controls are excluded.

sources.title: Set scaling rules in Azure Container Apps
sources.shortSummary: Documents replica limits, HTTP/TCP/custom KEDA rules, Azure identity authentication, scale-to-zero conditions, and unsupported vertical scaling.

sources.title: Health probes in Azure Container Apps
sources.shortSummary: Documents startup/readiness/liveness probes, HTTP/TCP behavior, and restrictions on exec, named ports, and gRPC.

sources.title: Use the Azure Key Vault provider for Secrets Store CSI Driver in an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) cluster
sources.shortSummary: Documents Key Vault CSI volumes, SecretProviderClass, identity requirements, and the subPath limitation for automatic secret updates.

sources.title: Vector search in Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL
sources.shortSummary: Defines embedding path/type/dimension/distance policies, vector index choices, and VectorDistance retrieval. Expanded high-scale private-preview capabilities are excluded.

sources.title: Indexing policies in Azure Cosmos DB
sources.shortSummary: Defines index path inclusion, specificity, composite sorting/filtering, vector indexes, and online index-policy transformation.

sources.title: Consistency levels in Azure Cosmos DB
sources.shortSummary: Defines the five read consistency contracts, session-token scope, throughput tradeoffs, and strong-consistency multiwrite restrictions.

sources.title: Change feed processor in Azure Cosmos DB
sources.shortSummary: Documents .NET/Java processor SDK support, lease ownership/checkpoints, scaling, at-least-once processing, and initial start position. Python pull reads are not the processor SDK.

sources.title: Optimize performance when using pgvector in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server
sources.shortSummary: Uses EXPLAIN, parallel workers, dimensioned vector indexes, matching operator classes, partial indexes, and partitioning to optimize pgvector retrieval.

sources.title: PgBouncer in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server
sources.shortSummary: Documents integrated PgBouncer, port 6432, transaction-pooling settings, supported compute tiers, failover behavior, and connection diagnostics. Preview total-client-connections metric is excluded.

sources.title: What are vector embeddings and vector search in Azure Managed Redis?
sources.shortSummary: Documents provisioning RediSearch with Enterprise clustering and NoEviction, vector storage in hash/JSON data, and exact versus approximate retrieval. Replaces the failed how-to URL.

sources.title: Use Redis modules with Azure Managed Redis
sources.shortSummary: Documents provisioning-time Redis module selection and RediSearch/RedisJSON capabilities; modules cannot be added later.

sources.title: Message transfers, locks, and settlement
sources.shortSummary: Defines ReceiveAndDelete versus PeekLock, settlement operations, lock renewal, and the need to handle uncertain outcomes and duplicate processing.

sources.title: Overview of Service Bus dead-letter queues
sources.shortSummary: Distinguishes normal and transfer DLQs, conditional TTL dead-lettering, delivery-count failures, deferred messages, and resubmission after repair.

sources.title: CloudEvents v1.0 schema with Azure Event Grid
sources.shortSummary: Documents CloudEvents input/output configuration and schema compatibility without treating payload shape as delivery guarantees.

sources.title: Understand event filtering for Event Grid subscriptions
sources.shortSummary: Defines event type, subject, and typed advanced filters, including OR within values and AND across filters.

sources.title: Event Grid message delivery and retry
sources.shortSummary: Documents at-least-once delivery, nonretryable response codes, attempt/TTL limits, output batching, and optional Blob dead-lettering.

sources.title: Authentication and authorization with Microsoft Entra ID
sources.shortSummary: Separates publisher authentication from the events/send/action authorization granted by Event Grid Data Sender. Preview disable-local-auth examples are excluded.

sources.title: Azure Functions developer reference guide for Python apps
sources.shortSummary: Documents Python decorator versus function.json models, project files, blueprints, environment settings, dependencies, and deployment boundaries.

sources.title: Azure Functions triggers and bindings
sources.shortSummary: Defines triggers, optional bindings, language-specific declarations, supported directionality, and SDK access when binding capabilities are insufficient.

sources.title: Azure Functions developer guide
sources.shortSummary: Defines function-app deployment scope, host storage, binding connection configuration, and local versus hosted identities.

sources.title: Azure Functions hosting options
sources.shortSummary: Compares hosting plans, scale behavior, execution/HTTP timeout boundaries, always-ready options, and plan-specific resource limits.

sources.title: About Azure Key Vault secrets
sources.shortSummary: Distinguishes encrypted secret storage, enabled/validity attributes, and permitted GET operations for expired or not-yet-valid secrets.

sources.title: Azure Key Vault service limits
sources.shortSummary: Distinguishes object count from transaction throttling and separates vault from Managed HSM limits.

sources.title: Quickstart: Create a Python app with Azure App Configuration
sources.shortSummary: Shows Python-provider loading into a mapping, identity-based access, and integration with application configuration.

sources.title: Enable Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry for .NET, Node.js, Python, and Java applications
sources.shortSummary: Documents supported language instrumentation and actual data-flow verification; points to per-feature release status instead of implying all OTel features are GA.

sources.title: Add and modify Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry for .NET, Java, Node.js, and Python applications
sources.shortSummary: Documents custom operation spans, attributes, exception capture, and trace/span identity; GenAI feedback extensions are outside scope.

sources.title: Configure Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry
sources.shortSummary: Documents connection targeting, service resource attributes, trace sampling, telemetry persistence/retries, and query-string redaction with language-specific settings.

sources.title: Log queries in Azure Monitor
sources.shortSummary: Establishes Azure Monitor's KQL basis and its differences from Azure Data Explorer rather than assuming every Kusto operator is available.
